Package neqsim.thermo.util.mineral

Class MineralH2SBuffers

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.util.mineral.MineralH2SBuffers
public final class MineralH2SBuffers extends Object
Catalogue of mineral-fluid reactions that can buffer or generate H2S in petroleum reservoirs.

Each reaction is atom-balanced (checked on construction) and uses the CH4/CO2 pair of the reservoir fluid as redox agent, so the equilibrium H2S fugacity follows from the fluid itself without an assumed hydrogen or oxygen fugacity. Liquid water enters as a condensed species with activity (set brine water activity with SolidGasReactionEquilibrium.setActivity(String, double)). Use SolidGasReactionEquilibrium.solveForGas(neqsim.thermo.system.SystemInterface, String) with target "H2S".

Reactions and the buffered H2S fugacity
Key Reaction f(H2S) proportional to
pyrite-pyrrhotite 4 FeS2 + CH4 + 2 H2O = 4 FeS + 4 H2S + CO2 (K f(CH4)/f(CO2))^(1/4)
pyrite-siderite 4 FeS2 + CH4 + 3 CO2 + 6 H2O = 4 FeCO3 + 8 H2S (K f(CH4) f(CO2)^3)^(1/8)
pyrite-magnetite 6 FeS2 + CH4 + 10 H2O = 2 Fe3O4 + 12 H2S + CO2 (K f(CH4)/f(CO2))^(1/12)
pyrrhotite-magnetite 12 FeS + CO2 + 14 H2O = 4 Fe3O4 + 12 H2S + CH4 (K f(CO2)/f(CH4))^(1/12)
pyrrhotite-siderite FeS + CO2 + H2O = FeCO3 + H2S K f(CO2)
anhydrite-TSR CaSO4 + CH4 = CaCO3 + H2S + H2O K f(CH4) (thermodynamic limit of sulfate reduction)

Troilite stands in for pyrrhotite. The equilibria are thermodynamic limits; whether a buffer controls a reservoir depends on which minerals coexist with the fluid and on reaction rates.

      public static SolidGasReactionEquilibrium anhydriteSulfateReduction()
      Overall thermochemical sulfate reduction by methane: CaSO4 + CH4 = CaCO3 + H2S + H2O(l). Its equilibrium lies far to the right, so H2S from this route is controlled by kinetics and sulfate supply, not by equilibrium.
      Returns:

    • sideriteMagnetite

      public static SolidGasReactionEquilibrium sideriteMagnetite()
      Siderite-magnetite boundary (no sulfur): 12 FeCO3 + 2 H2O(l) = 4 Fe3O4 + 11 CO2 + CH4. Fixes the CO2 fugacity at which siderite and magnetite coexist for a given CH4 fugacity; used for mineral stability diagrams. Not part of all() because it does not involve H2S.
      Returns:
      reaction
